\renewcommand{\ResultsBody}{Adaptation in this regime is worth 1.186$\times$: the clairvoyant switch reaches $L=21.267$ where the best \emph{fixed} law in hindsight reaches $25.229$ and the frozen rule $27.972$. That is the budget every arm below is competing for, and it is small---which is worth saying plainly, because a $14\%$ ceiling sets the scale for how large any component effect can honestly be.

With no harness at all the regent reaches $\Rreg=0.934$; with all three channels, $\Rreg=1.125$. Neither figure should be read as the harness being unnecessary: an arm with no channel still sees the current state at each review, so it can respond to prevalence even though it cannot learn that its instrument stopped working.

The factorial (\cref{tab:factorial}) attributes the difference to memory, which made the regent \emph{worse}. Terms not listed did not survive Holm correction across the family of 7 effects.

This design's minimum detectable effect, computed from the observed per-seed spread at the Holm-corrected $\alpha$ and $80\%$ power, is 0.29 loss units against a total adaptation budget of 3.96. It can therefore resolve a component only if that component is worth at least 7\% of everything adaptation is worth in this regime. The null below rules out large component effects and does \emph{not} rule out modest ones; halving the detectable effect would require $n=80$ seeds.}
